title: Tudok..., Nem tudok...: Ability and Its Limits

sections.title: Bringing the first half of Unit 23 together
sections.content: tud + infinitive states a personal skill and conjugates for every person: tudok, tudsz, tud, tudunk, tudtok, tudnak. jól/rosszul in front of tud grades that skill. To negate it, negate the conjugated tud itself, and add mert to explain why — the missing piece is always something about the PERSON: never learned, no license, no talent.

sections.title: tud, graded and negated
rows: Nem tudok úszni, mert sosem tanultam.
I can't swim, because I never learned.
Petra nem tud vezetni, mert nincs jogosítványa.
Petra can't drive, because she doesn't have a license.

items.spanish: Zsófia ügyes: tud rajzolni, főzni és zongorázni is.
items.english: Zsófia is skilled: she can draw, cook, and play the piano too.

items.spanish: Ildikó nagyon jól tud főzni, Gábor rosszul.
items.english: Ildikó cooks very well; Gábor cooks badly.

items.spanish: Petra tud úszni, de ma nem lehet, mert zárva van az uszoda.
items.english: Petra can swim (she has the ability), but today it's not possible (the pool is closed).

sections.content: nem tud (about YOUR ability) is different from nem lehet (about the SITUATION) — Petra can swim, but today it's not possible, because the pool is closed. Keep asking whose limit you're describing.
